business_scope.primary_industry_name: International Tax Structuring and Transfer Pricing Advisory

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Sultanate of Oman (Muscat Governorate as the registered-office reference; unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax authority)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – Civil Law based on statutory codes and Royal Decrees, with Islamic Sharia as a foundational source of legislation
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Oman–United States Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 January 2009)
Oman–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (2016, in force 2017)
Oman–Pakistan Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1997)
GCC Unified Economic Agreement (1981) and GCC Common Market provisions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Royal Decree No. 30/2016 (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism Law); Central Bank of Oman Executive Regulations on AML/CFT (2020); Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree No. 18/2019, as amended); ministerial implementing decisions of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion on the Beneficial Ownership Register; oversight by the National Committee for Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Incumbency) of the foreign parent entity
Notarized board resolution authorizing incorporation of the Omani Single Person Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign parent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof-of-address of all UBOs, directors, and the SPC general manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consular authority of the passport-holder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (KYC/UBO confirmation) for the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank of the foreign parent entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Charter) of the foreign parent company

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all natural-person UBOs, shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, and the SPC manager against: (i) the consolidated sanctions list of the National Committee for Combating Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists as communicated by the Omani Ministry of Foreign Affairs; (iii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; and (iv) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Screening must be completed no later than 24 hours prior to submission of the incorporation dossier and repeated at banking onboarding. A written Compliance Screen Report must be produced, retained for at least five years per Article 26 of Royal Decree No. 30/2016, and produced to the Ministry or the Financial Intelligence Unit upon request.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Invest Easy (استثمر بسهولة) – https://investeasy.gov.om, operated by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be submitted in Arabic (mandatory) and may include an English/Latin-script transliteration; the legal-form suffix 'Single Person Company (SPC)' / 'شركة الشخص الواحد' must be appended; the transliteration must be phonetically compatible with the Arabic original and must not be misleading, offensive, or conflict with registered names; non-English foreign-script components require prior ministerial approval.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Muscat (where it implies municipal or state franchise)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit an administrative reconsideration request through the Invest Easy 'Complaints and Appeals' channel or by written petition to the Commercial Registration Department within 15 working days of the rejection notice, attaching the original rejection notification, the name-clearance application receipt, and a legal memorandum addressing the cited grounds. The Ministry must issue a decision within 30 working days. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an annulment action before the Administrative Court under the Administrative Judiciary Law (Royal Decree No. 26/2020) within 60 days of the final administrative decision. A fresh name-clearance application may be resubmitted only after exhaustion of the appeal or after the statutory decision period has lapsed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are not accepted for the statutory registered-office requirement. A serviced business-centre arrangement providing a physical desk, meeting facilities, and local management presence is acceptable in Muscat for low-risk professional-services companies. A PO Box alone is insufficient and will trigger a compliance objection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium – approximately 35% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation. Probability rises to approximately 60% upon application for government procurement, tax registration, or investment-incentive schemes. Unannounced inspections are typically triggered by FIU suspicious-transaction alerts, commercial-registration renewal, municipality license audits, or inter-agency random inspections.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Oman Commercial Companies Law, Royal Decree No. 18/2019, in particular Articles 1, 10, 26-29 and Chapter VI regarding Single Person Companies (A.H.S.); executive regulations issued by Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MCIIP).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MCIIP) - Commercial Registry, Sultanate of Oman; e-filing through Invest Oman or MCIIP e-services portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Single Person Company, together with Commercial Registration Application and the shareholder's written consent in lieu of a general assembly.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Single Person Company under Royal Decree No. 18/2019; however the subscribed capital must be fully paid at incorporation and must be adequate for the intended consultancy operations. No escrow account or capital deposit certificate is required by the Companies Law for this commercial professional services activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the incorporation documents and Memorandum and Articles of Association of the Single Person Company, as submitted to the Commercial Registry, are hereby ratified and adopted; (2) the paid-up share capital as set out in the Memorandum is approved and deemed fully subscribed; (3) the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at the address specified in the registration file; (4) the person named in the registration as Manager/Director is appointed to such office with full authority to represent the Company and open bank accounts; and (5) the Company shall procure all post-incorporation licenses, tax registrations and social insurance enrollments required for lawful operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIIP Commercial Registry via Invest Oman / MCIIP e-Services portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Applicant submits two to three Arabic and/or English proposed names through the MCIIP online commercial name reservation system. The system checks conflict and obscene names under Oman Commercial Registry practice. Once approved, the name reservation certificate is generated and is valid for thirty days. Payment of the name reservation fee is made online.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application
Passport or commercial registration copy of ultimate foreign shareholder
Power of attorney if filed by a corporate services agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, applicant may refile with modified names or appeal the decision to the MCIIP Commercial Registration Directorate within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public, Ministry of Justice (Oman); legalization by Ministry of Foreign Affairs for foreign corporate instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Sole Shareholder executes the Arabic-language Memorandum and Articles of Association and the Single Person Company declaration. For a foreign corporate parent, the parent's board resolution and power of attorney must be legalized, apostilled or chain-certified as required by Omani practice. The Notary Public verifies identities, capacity and authority, then attests the instrument for submission to the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Board resolution of foreign corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation
Power of attorney in favor of local agent or signatory
Passport or national identity cards of all signatories
Certificate of good standing or incorporation certificate of shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a defect in the draft or authority documentation, correct the instrument and re-submit to the same notary within three working days; no additional court proceeding is required for minor drafting adjustments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Issuance of Certificate of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, name reservation certificate, completed Commercial Registration Application and lease evidence are uploaded to the MCIIP portal. The Commercial Registry officer reviews the data, confirms the SPC share structure, enters the company in the Commercial Register and issues the Commercial Registration Certificate and company identity card.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name reservation certificate
Commercial Registration Application signed by shareholder or authorized agent
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or landlord consent)
Foreign shareholder corporate records and incumbency certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for defective information, respond to the 'notice of forms' within 15 working days; refile corrected signatures or documents online without new fees except any applicable correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Oman Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Tax Authority (OTA) - Taxpayer Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After commercial registration, the company must register for income tax in accordance with Oman Income Tax Law (Royal Decree 28/2009 as amended). The application is submitted on OTA online services with the Commercial Registration number. If taxable turnover is expected to exceed OMR 38,500 per annum, the company must simultaneously apply for value-added tax registration under the GCC VAT Law applicable in Oman.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Lease contract and registered office proof
Passport of shareholders and directors
Bank account details or acknowledgement from the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If OTA requests additional support documents, provide translations or clarifications within 14 calendar days through the e-portfolio; if the request is not satisfied, the company may appeal an OTA default assessment under the procedural rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration with Public Authority for Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The SPC must register as an employer with PASI as soon as it has actual employees. The company submits the employer registration form, the Commercial Registration number and employment contracts. Newly hired Omanis and Gulf nationals must be enrolled for occupational injury and pension coverage; expatriates are registered for the private sector insurance schemes as applicable.
required_dossiers: Employer registration form
Commercial Registration Certificate
Registered office lease
List of employees and civil ID or passport copies
Employment contracts for initial staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If PASI issues a demand for penalties, the company may submit a compliance affidavit with backdated payroll records and request waiver of administrative fines for first-time late registration; continuing objection may be filed to PASI appellate committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License for Professional Consultancy Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Muscat Municipality; for other governorates, the respective Wilayat/Directorate of Municipality, Municipality Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Commercial Registration, the company applies for the Municipal Operating License for a professional office. The applicant submits the lease agreement, a floor plan, proof of CR and tax ID, and any required fire safety and environmental checklist to the municipal business licensing window. Approval results in the physical operating license required to open the office and conduct client consultations.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Lease agreement or title deed for premises
Floor plan and use of premises description
Civil defense preliminary approval or letter
No-objection certificate from any commercial complex owner/management
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If zoning or land use restrictions apply, the company may request a change-of-use permit from the Municipality; any refusal must be notified in writing and may be appealed to the Municipal Review Committee within 30 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense Inspection and Corporate Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Civil Defense, Royal Oman Police; licensed commercial bank in Oman
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company invites the Civil Defense inspector to inspect the office premises for fire safety compliance, emergency exits, extinguishers, and electrical load safety. Upon successful inspection, the Civil Defense approval certificate is issued. Using the CR, tax ID and notarized board powers, the bank account is opened and documentary evidence is retained for Oman regulatory compliance.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Civil Defense inspection application and layout plan
Passport and tax ID of signatories
Bank KYC forms, board resolution, and corporate due diligence records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Civil Defense flags fire or safety deficiencies, the company has 5 working days to install corrective equipment and schedule a re-inspection; bank may request complementary documentary evidence of registered office and business licensing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MCIIP) - Commercial Licensing Directorate, Muscat Municipality or relevant Wilayat Municipality, in coordination with Oman Tax Authority and Ministry of Labour.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Operating License for Professional Consultancy Services (Commercial License for Management and Tax Advisory Office) issued under the Commercial Registration Certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Authority, Sultanate of Oman (previously Ministry of Environment and Climate Affairs)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 4 (office-based non-industrial service activity); no full EIA Study or Initial Environmental Evaluation is required. Subsequent change of activity to industrial or laboratory scale would require a Category 2 or Category 3 assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office premises must discharge sanitary wastewater only to the municipal sewer network in compliance with Muscat Municipality wastewater discharge standards and Oman Standard OS 8/2016; waste handling must follow municipal segregated waste guidelines and Omani Standard OS 211/2017; no industrial atmospheric emissions, VOCs, or trade waste are generated by this consultancy activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from General Directorate of Civil Defense (Royal Oman Police), fire extinguisher maintenance and emergency exit conformity; structural load inspection certificate issued by the building owner or municipality confirming approved office occupancy load; occupational health and workplace clearance from Ministry of Labour for the number of office employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Oman Tax Authority (OTA) — national revenue administration succeeding the Secretariat General of Taxation of the Ministry of Finance; statutory e-portal for income tax, VAT, withholding declarations, and e-invoicing clearance: www.taxoman.gov.om, integrated with the Bayan national customs single window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign investors must first incorporate the SPC at the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) and obtain the Commercial Registration (CR). With the CR issued, the SPC must register for Corporate Income Tax with the OTA within three months from commencement of business activity to obtain the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN / tax card). A non-resident company carrying on activities through an Omani permanent establishment (PE) or deriving Omani-source income without a local office must itself register with the OTA and, where required, instruct an Omani tax agent. VAT registration is effected separately through the same OTA e-portal: within 30 days after taxable supplies or imports cross the mandatory OMR 38,500 annual threshold, or voluntarily at OMR 19,250, the OTA issues a distinct 15-digit VAT TIN. The Omani SPC must also file a tax clearance / no-objection certificate before CR cancellation, share transfer, or cessation of activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — mandatory for an Omani SPC; the single-person limited company is an opaque resident corporate taxpayer, not eligible for pass-through or partnership classification. Territorial_Scope — resident SPC is taxed on worldwide income at the 15% CIT headline rate, with a 0% band on the first OMR 100,000 of taxable income; non-resident persons and foreign PEs are taxed on Oman-source income only, with outward dividends, interest, royalties, and management/technical fees subject to 10% withholding tax unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Treaty. Tax_Exempt_Zone — available only where the SPC obtains a licence in a designated free or economic zone (e.g., Duqm SEZAD, Sohar Port and Freezone, Salalah Free Zone), in which case zone incentive laws provide defined multi-year CIT holidays and special VAT treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box, hybrid-mismatch, fiscal unity, or transparent-entity election exists under Omani law; the SPC is per se taxable. Available statutory elections and options include: (i) the 0% CIT band election for taxable income not exceeding OMR 100,000 per year; (ii) voluntary VAT registration at the OMR 19,250 threshold; (iii) VAT grouping between affiliated entities subject to OTA pre-approval and joint-and-several liability; (iv) accounting-period alignment election to align the Omani subsidiary with the ultimate foreign parent's reporting year; (v) income-tax loss carryforward utilisation election within the statutory five-year limitation window. No group relief or loss-transfer regime is recognised.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — implemented under the GCC Unified VAT Agreement and the Omani VAT Law (Royal Decree No. 121/2020) together with VAT Executive Regulations; no separate sales-and-use tax or goods-and-services tax applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: OMR 38,500 of annual taxable supplies during any consecutive 12-month period, or OMR 38,500 of cumulative imports into Oman in the same window (approximately USD 100,100 at the pegged exchange rate of OMR 1 = USD 2.6008). Voluntary registration: OMR 19,250 of annual taxable supplies or taxable expenses. Non-resident suppliers of distance sales or electronically supplied services to Omani customers must register at the mandatory threshold unless a VAT representative has been appointed and the place-of-supply rules allocate taxation elsewhere in the GCC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Oman has introduced a phased national e-invoicing mandate under the OTA. VAT-registered persons in the designated tranches must issue e-invoices in a machine-readable structured XML format, transmit invoices to the OTA's e-invoice clearance portal in near real time before issuance to the buyer, obtain an approved clearance identifier, and affix a cryptographic QR code / digital stamp. Businesses integrate their ERP and billing systems with the OTA-approved API communication protocol; B2G and large-taxpayer waves are first in sequence, with subsequent rollout for all VAT registrants. Paper invoices remain lawful outside the active waves, but once the mandate applies, an unrecorded or un-cleared invoice is inadmissible as a VAT recovery document, input tax is denied, and qualifying export documentation must be linked digitally to the Bayan customs records and archived for OTA audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies where title and physical possession pass to a non-resident buyer, the goods are consigned to a destination outside Oman and outside the GCC Implementing States, export is completed within 90 days from the date of supply, and the supplier retains a valid Customs Export Declaration, commercial invoice, transport documents, and payment evidence. Services: zero-rating applies to (i) international transport of passengers and goods; (ii) services directly connected with exported goods, such as loading, handling, freight, inspection, and marine insurance; and (iii) services supplied to a non-resident customer that are effectively consumed and benefit outside Oman and the GCC. For the cross-border tax-structuring advisory SPC, zero-rating is permitted only where the consultancy is performed and used entirely outside Omani territory, the recipient is outside the GCC, no Omani PE or fixed base is involved, and no application of the advice occurs inside Oman; advisory services evaluating or implementing Omani domestic structures remain taxable at the standard 5% rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayan national single-window record) evidencing physical export from an Omani port, free zone, or approved customs territory
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Multimodal Transport Document showing despatch to a destination outside Oman and the GCC Implementing States
Commercial Invoice containing the zero-rating statement, the exporter and consignee VAT/TIN identifiers, Incoterms, and the unique customs reference (UCR)
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank-issued, cross-referenced to SWIFT MT103/MT202) evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the repatriation benchmark
Packing list, cargo manifest, and freight-forwarder or insurer certification where multimodal or indirect export movement has been used
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are a priority audit area for the OTA. Unsupported, late-filed, or fictitious export substantiation exposes the exporter to retrospective VAT assessment at the standard 5% rate with late-payment penalties of 1% per month of the unpaid tax, fixed administrative fines ranging from OMR 500 to OMR 10,000 per defective document, denial of input VAT recovery, and suspension of pending refunds. Where the Authority establishes deliberate fraud — including false export declarations, circular fund flows, or re-introduction of exported goods into Oman — the clawback period extends to the statutory limitation period, criminal fines up to OMR 20,000 or double the evaded tax may be imposed, and responsible directors or officers may be imprisoned for up to three years. Refunds founded on zero-rated export transactions are auditable within the limitation window and are automatically frozen while a tax dispute is under review or objection.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Oman (CBO) - the sole monetary authority, banking supervisor and official foreign-exchange administrator of the Sultanate of Oman; the CBO Banking Supervision Department regulates licensed banks and the CBO Financial Intelligence Unit exercises the national AML/CFT enforcement mandate, complemented for remittances by the Oman Tax Authority (tax clearance) and MOCIIP (Foreign Capital Investment Law registration). Legal basis: Banking Law (RD 114/2000), AML Law (RD 30/2016) and CBO foreign-exchange directives.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Oman is a fully convertible current-account jurisdiction under IMF Article VIII, without exchange controls on payments and transfers for trade in goods or services or on profit and capital remittances by a 100% foreign-owned SPC. The OMR is pegged to the US dollar at the CBO reference rate of US$1 = OMR 0.3845 with a narrow intervention band, eliminating material USD/OMR risk and ensuring on-demand convertibility. Capital-account operations are generally open, subject to CBO statistical reporting; practical profit-remittance hurdles are documentary rather than regulatory, requiring audited accounts, treasury validation of the commercial reality, tax-clearance confirmation and, where a double-taxation treaty is invoked, the relevant residence certificate and relief form.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no export-proceeds surrender obligation in Omani law: the mandatory conversion ratio is 0% and there is no statutory repatriation deadline. Exporters may retain 100% of export receipts in foreign-currency accounts at CBO-licensed banks, provided each receipt is received through the banking system and captured in CBO Balance-of-Payments reporting. For an ISIC 7020 consultancy SPC, foreign-currency fee collections may lawfully be held offshore or swept into the Omani operational account without conversion penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow / share-capital deposit and multi-currency operational account (OMR, USD, EUR, GBP)
Operational current account with multi-currency sweep and cross-border trade/FX line
Operational current account (OMR/USD) for domestic collections and payments
Operational current account and term deposit (OMR/USD)
Operational current account (OMR) for local disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP) — Commercial Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the Commercial Register issuance anniversary; renewal window opens 30 days prior to expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal fine of OMR 10 per month (approx. USD 26); failure to renew for more than 12 months may trigger administrative strike-off of the SPC by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the tax year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, on or before 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of OMR 100 (approx. USD 260) or 10% of tax assessed, whichever is greater; additional late-payment charge of 1% per month on unpaid tax; persistent non-filing may lead to automatic assessment and enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Financial Statements and Independent Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Oman Tax Authority (attached to the annual tax return); auditor licensed by the Oman Capital Market Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, in conjunction with the corporate income tax return; by 30 April for calendar-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A tax return filed without the required audited financial statements is deemed defective and attracts the general late-filing penalty of OMR 100 (approx. USD 260) or 10% of tax due, whichever is greater; a qualified or adverse audit opinion likewise exposes the filing to OTA scrutiny.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (UBO Register Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MoCIIP — Commercial Registrar via Invest Oman e-Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, concurrent with the Commercial Register renewal; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 15 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of OMR 100 to OMR 500 (approx. USD 260 to 1,300) for inaccurate or late UBO filings; Commercial Register renewal may be withheld until compliance is restored.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all Omani commercial companies irrespective of size; an SPC must appoint an OCA-licensed auditor. For tax purposes, audited financial statements are compulsory where gross income exceeds OMR 50,000 (approx. USD 130,000) in a tax year; below this threshold, reviewed or unaudited statements may be accepted by OTA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted in Oman; no separate Local GAAP exists.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SPC must file an annual UBO confirmation with MoCIIP at the time of Commercial Register renewal. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership — a natural person holding or controlling more than 25% directly or indirectly — must be reported to the Registrar within 15 days. The on-site UBO register must be continuously maintained and reconciled with the filed confirmation.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Oman levies a flat corporate income tax rate of 15 percent on taxable income under Article 33 of the Income Tax Law (Royal Decree 28/2009, as amended by Royal Decree 9/2017). No reduced small-business bracket currently applies to management consultancy SPCs. Targeted incentives exist for strategic projects, tourism, agriculture, fisheries and export-oriented manufacturing by royal decree or ministerial decision, typically as 5-to-10-year partial or full CIT holidays. SPCs licensed in the Duqm Special Economic Zone may obtain a 30-year CIT holiday conditional on real economic substance and prior OTA certification; Salalah and Sohar free zone entities may enjoy 10-to-30-year holidays as individually granted. ISIC 7020 tax structuring advisory services do not independently qualify for sector-based exemptions, so the practical effective rate for a standard foreign-owned SPC is 15 percent on accounting profits adjusted for non-deductible items.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 2 (SPC / Company), filed electronically through the Oman Tax Authority (OTA) e-Services portal at tax.gov.om under the taxpayer's Tax Card number (TIN). Audited financial statements must be attached where the SPC's annual turnover or capital exceeds OMR 500,000 or where the OTA requires assurance; unaudited management accounts are unacceptable for losses or large related-party transactions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The SPC files one comprehensive return per tax year (financial year). Withholding agents also file separate quarterly WHT returns (Form No. 4) within 15 days of each quarter-end, reconciling amounts withheld on payments to non-residents.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within four months after the end of the SPC's financial year; for calendar-year companies the deadline is 30 April. A written extension of up to one additional month may be granted by the OTA if application is made before the original due date. Payment of the final liability is due on the same deadline; deferred payment accrues a 1 percent monthly late-payment surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique 15-digit OTA taxpayer identification number assigned at incorporation or foreign registration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with a permanent establishment or Omani business licence enter their Oman TIN; entities only earning Omani-source passive income do not file this form and instead suffer WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Legal Form and Commercial Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form indicator (select Single Person Company) and the CR number issued by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign holding companies operating through a branch select the branch/PE indicator and enter the branch registration number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax Period (Start and End Dates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The financial year covered by the return; must match the period in the approved financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Branch tax years follow the foreign head office financial year unless a different period is approved by the OTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from management consultancy, tax structuring fees, and all other operating income before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents include only Oman-source revenue attributed to the local PE; off-shore structuring fees not sourced to Oman are excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Direct Costs and Deductible Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, rent, professional indemnity insurance, software subscriptions, travel, and other allowable costs matched to the revenue period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office cost allocations are deductible only under the arm's-length principle with TP documentation and evidence of actual economic contribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory add-backs: fines, bribes, dividends distributed, excessive entertainment, disallowed interest, tax-related provisions, and capital expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include payments to foreign related parties where no TP file exists; the OTA may recharacterize them as constructive dividends or royalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Taxable Income Before Loss Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit adjusted by Box 5 and Box 6 entries; the starting point for CIT at 15 percent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident PEs, use the attributable profit in the Oman branch accounts rather than the worldwide profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unrelieved tax losses from prior years, deductible within the 5-year carryforward limit, subject to continuity of ownership and business activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches may carry forward losses only against future Oman-source PE income while the PE activity continues.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deducting loss relief; the base on which the 15 percent CIT is computed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is nil or negative, the SPC still files the return to register the loss; a nil return with activity may trigger OTA queries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Auto-calculated 15 percent charge on Box 9; any treaty-derived adjustments must be separately disclosed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty rate reductions are not applied in this box; they are claimed through the WHT relief protocol or amended assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Withholding Tax Credits and Advance Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for Omani WHT suffered on income received from customers, plus any voluntary advance tax deposits paid through the portal.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents credit only Omani WHT; foreign taxes are not creditable against Oman CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Net Tax Payable or Refund Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final settlement: Box 10 minus Box 11; refunds are processed by OTA after verification of the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments must be routed through an Omani bank account in the taxpayer's name; refunds to non-resident accounts require OTA approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 - Declaration and Legal Representative Signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed declaration by the SPC manager or authorized director confirming the return is complete and accurate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The named signatory assumes personal criminal liability for false declarations; a power of attorney should be registered with the OTA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of 25 percent of the tax due, subject to a statutory minimum and maximum that the OTA applies, plus a 1 percent monthly surcharge on unpaid tax. Defective or misleading returns attract additional OTA-imposed fines up to OMR 10,000. Continued non-filing triggers best-of-judgment assessment, suspension of the tax card, blocking of government licences, and criminal referral for evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Oman does not impose any statutory withholding tax on dividends, profit distributions, or branch profit remittances to resident or non-resident shareholders. The absence of DWT is a deliberate fiscal policy to attract foreign capital; therefore no domestic withholding obstacle exists for an SPC repatriating dividends to its foreign parent. The transfer must still be supported by audited distributable reserves and board minutes to avoid reclassification as a loan or undeclared remuneration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Oman has an extensive DTA network (over 40 treaties). To invoke treaty benefits for cross-border payments, the non-resident recipient must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the residence-state tax authority covering the payment year; (ii) complete the OTA treaty-relief application (WHT-1 or the corresponding e-service through the OTA portal) attaching the TRC, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and the underlying contract; (iii) deliver the OTA approval or certified exemption to the Omani payer before payment so the payer avoids deducting WHT; (iv) where WHT has already been deducted, file a refund claim with the OTA through the annual return or a stand-alone refund application within the statutory limitation period (generally four years from the tax year end). The OTA applies a substance-over-form test; a mere letterbox company in the treaty state is denied relief under the principal purpose test aligned with the OECD Multilateral Instrument.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law (Income Tax Law, Article 15): 10 percent WHT applies to gross Omani-source royalties, interest, and technical or management service fees paid by an Omani resident (including an SPC) to a non-resident without a PE. Treaty rates vary: Oman's DTAs generally reduce royalties and interest to 10 percent (e.g., India-Oman, UK-Oman, France-Oman), with certain treaties allowing 0 percent on interest paid to financial institutions or governments. Where a treaty provides a lower rate, the payer must have received OTA treaty-relief approval before payment; otherwise the 10 percent WHT is withheld and the recipient claims refund. Payments for tax structuring consultancy are scrutinized as 'services performed in Oman'; if the service renders economic value within Oman, the 10 percent WHT applies regardless of where the invoice is issued. Transactions characterized as management fees paid to an intangibles-rich parent also face TP recharacterization as constructive royalties or dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Oman Transfer Pricing Regulations (Ministerial Decision No. 57/2023), effective for tax years beginning on or after 1 January 2024, impose: (i) Local File obligation where the aggregate annual value of controlled transactions with related parties equals or exceeds OMR 500,000; (ii) Master File obligation where the multinational group's consolidated worldwide revenue equals or exceeds OMR 50 million; (iii) Country-by-Country Report and notification where the MNE group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds OMR 375 million. A listed taxpayer must also file a TP disclosure statement with the annual CIT return when controlled transactions exceed OMR 500,000. Even below the thresholds, a written TP policy and contemporaneous benchmarking must be made available to the OTA on request within 30 days; the SPC is required to be ready to demonstrate arm's-length pricing for all cross-border management fees, advisory fees and cost recharges.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Oman does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations filing regime, but economic substance is embedded in multiple legal layers. The Commercial Companies Law (Royal Decree 18/2019) requires every SPC to maintain a registered office in Oman, a resident manager, board decision-making records, local bank accounts, payroll, and physical premises consistent with its licensed activity. For ISIC 7020 tax structuring services, the OTA will evaluate substance by evidence of actual consultancy work performed in Oman, qualified professional staff, execution of engagement letters, and control over cross-border transactions. The Tax Procedures Law (Royal Decree 31/2023) contains a General Anti-Avoidance Rule and substance-based recharacterization powers, and Oman's commitment to the OECD BEPS framework means shell companies with no local decision-making are disregarded, with profits reattributed to the ultimate parent jurisdiction. The OTA may also deny treaty benefits under the principal purpose test if the SPC was created primarily to obtain Omani tax benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of consultancy revenue, false invoicing, destruction of accounting records, submission of forged tax returns, or concealment of foreign bank accounts from the OTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Procedures Law (RD 31/2023) and Income Tax Law: imprisonment up to five years, fines up to OMR 100,000, confiscation of proceeds, assessment of all evaded tax, a 25 percent evasion penalty, and a 1 percent monthly late-payment surcharge. The OTA is empowered to publish the names of convicted evaders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SPC manager, directors, and controlling shareholders shadow-direct the entity are personally exposed: criminal conviction on Gross Negligence grounds, civil restitution of the full evaded tax, OTA-issued travel bans, seizure of personal assets, and disqualification from holding future board or management positions in Oman.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an Omani SPC with no office, staff, or real consultancy activity, used to route advisory fees, invoice offshore profits, or claim treaty benefits that were never economically earned in Oman.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization: the OTA disregards the SPC, reattributes profit to the foreign parent, denies all deductions claimed under the sham contract, imposes 15 percent CIT plus 1 percent monthly interest, and applies penal fines up to 50 percent of the additional tax. The company may also be struck off by the commercial registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: shareholders who authorized the sham structure are jointly and severally liable for the reattributed tax and penalties; directors face personal travel bans, confiscation of personal property, and imprisonment where the sham is coupled with fraudulent intent to evade tax or launder proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare the Local File, Master File, or CbCR despite crossing the OMR 500,000 / OMR 50 million / OMR 375 million thresholds; charging inflated group management fees to strip profits out of Oman; absence of contemporaneous TP benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties of up to OMR 20,000 for each missing or defective TP document, plus separate OMR 20,000 penalties for CbCR non-compliance; the OTA simultaneously makes an upward adjustment to taxable income, recharacterizes the fees as deemed dividends or royalties subject to 10 percent WHT, and adds the 1 percent monthly late-payment charge on the resulting CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign TP-out-of-scope disclaimers without factual basis face personal liability for the penalty where the documentation was knowingly false; travel bans and disqualification of the responsible chief financial officer or tax manager can be imposed by court order in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large cash fees for cross-border tax structuring without conducting customer due diligence, failing to maintain beneficial-ownership records, or structuring wire transfers below reporting thresholds to avoid suspicion (smurfing) in connection with wealth concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Oman's Anti-Money Laundering Law (RD 30/2016, as amended): imprisonment up to seven years, fines up to OMR 200,000, forfeiture of funds and instrumentalities, revocation of the commercial licence, and compulsory de-risking by Omani banks. The financial intelligence unit may freeze all SPC bank accounts pending investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML compliance is a statutory duty of the SPC manager and directors: personal criminal liability arises without proof of personal enrichment if the officer knew or should have known of the illicit funds; sanctions include sequestration of personal assets, travel bans, extradition exposure, and complete loss of the right to manage any Omani company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying royalties, interest, or technical service fees to a foreign parent without withholding the 10 percent WHT; failing to file the quarterly WHT return; making misrepresentations to avoid treaty withholding on payments routed through conduit jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the full un-withheld WHT from the payer, a penalty of 25 percent of the unrecovered amount, and the 1 percent monthly surcharge; the corresponding expense is disallowed for CIT purposes until evidence of the tax payment is produced; repeat offences trigger criminal fines and imprisonment of responsible officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors and the senior finance officer are jointly liable for the un-collected WHT as personal guarantors of corporate fiscal obligations; the OTA may seize personal bank accounts, issue travel bans, and extend criminal liability to all signatories of the payment instructions that circumvented the WHT regime.
